draft.title: Innovation
card: Innovation is a new or better product, or a new or better way of working. It can be a brand new idea or an improvement on something that already exists.
Product innovation
a new or improved good or service, such as an electric car or a home solar battery that stores power from rooftop panels.
Process innovation
a new or improved way of making or delivering things, such as a factory that uses robots to cut waste and save time.
An innovation can help a business stand out from rivals, cut costs and keep customers. Not every innovation succeeds, as buyers must want it at the price asked.
draft.remember: Innovation is something new or better, and it can help a business stand out from rivals, cut costs and keep customers.

a.q: A bakery wants to try something innovative. Which choice is an example of innovation?
opts: A bakery sells a new bread that keeps fresh for a week
A bakery changes its opening hours by one hour
A bakery repaints its shopfront the same colour
A bakery sells the same loaf at a slightly lower price
a.why: A bread that keeps fresh for a week is a new or better product. The other three are small changes to things the bakery already did, and none of them is a new or better product or way of working.
a.clue: Look for the option that gives buyers something new or better.

b.q: Ravi's farm near Shepparton buys sensors that tell him when each paddock needs water. He now uses far less water. What kind of innovation is this?
opts: A new way of working, because it changes how he farms
A new product, because he sells something new to buyers
Not innovation, because the farm still grows the same crop
Not innovation, because he bought the sensors from others
b.why: The sensors change how Ravi does his work, so this is a new way of working. The crop staying the same does not matter, because innovation can be a better way of working. It also does not matter that he did not invent the sensors.
b.clue: Ask what changed: what is sold, or how the work is done?

a.best: A bakery sells a new bread that keeps fresh for a week

b.best: A new way of working, because it changes how he farms

problems.detail: The right option is the longest and the only one with the word "new", which echoes the clue ("something new or better"). Two distractors say "the same". A student could pick it from the wording alone, without knowing the idea.

Process innovation

a.q: Which change at a bakery in Ballarat is an innovation?
opts: Baking a loaf that stays fresh for a whole week
Baking twice as many of its usual loaves each day
Charging fifty cents more for each of its loaves
Selling its usual loaves for less on Mondays
a.why: A loaf that stays fresh for a week is an improved product, so it is a product innovation. Baking more of the usual loaves, or changing their price, does not give buyers a better product or change how the work is done.
a.clue: Is the bakery improving something, or just selling more or at a different price?
